correctness.rationale: The normalized transform gives \(\widehat h(m)=q_m/p\), so translations of \(h\) are orthonormal and the two-dimensional Gabor Gram matrix factors into two Kronecker deltas. A vanishing value of \(h\) forces a length-\(p\) vanishing sum of \(p\)-th roots; the cyclotomic polynomial argument makes the exponent multiset a permutation, and the two modified exponents force the unique zero at residue \(1\). Thus the support has size \(p(p-1)\), which cannot tile \(\mathbb F_p^2\). Row supports prove nonproduct structure, Fourier conjugacy rules out nonnegative-real values, the norm and explicit value at zero rule out constant support modulus, and the quadratic Gauss-sum formula gives two distinct nonzero Fourier magnitudes.

final_claim: For every prime \(p\ge5\), the explicit quadratic row-shift window \(g(x,y)=p^{-1/2}h(x-y^2)\) generates a Gabor orthonormal basis on \(L^2(\mathbb F_p^2)\), has support of size \(p(p-1)\), and simultaneously satisfies all six nonproduct, nonpositive, nonconstant-modulus, unequal-cardinality, and nontiling properties asked for in the finite-prime-field Gabor-window question.
scientific_limitations: The construction is for primes \(p\ge5\) only.
It is an existence theorem, not a classification.
